summary: Market sentiment is mixed, with the Dow posting gains even as the AI trade shows signs of stress, reflected in Nvidia slipping from its position as the world's most valuable company to Apple reclaiming the top spot, signaling a rotation away from AI-driven momentum plays. The Federal Reserve remains a central macro focus, with markets closely monitoring anticipated remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, while Bitcoin ETFs snapping their inflow streak underscores growing sensitivity to the prospect of prolonged higher interest rates. At the sector level, tech is under pressure from AI trade skepticism — amplified by Nvidia's reported $250 billion backstep involving OpenAI's data center lease — while defensives and non-tech names are benefiting from the rotation, with Johnson & Johnson gaining on its talc settlement resolution and Coca-Cola earnings on deck as a consumer bellwether. Key risk factors include AI valuation sustainability, geopolitical tensions in West Asia keeping gold elevated, crude oil pricing in uncertainty around Iran peace prospects, and potential earnings disappointments prompting some investors to trim positions ahead of results. The short-term outlook remains cautious and stock-specific, with investors selectively buying dips in industrials and beaten-down chipmakers while awaiting clearer signals from Fed commentary and a wave of corporate earnings to determine whether the recent sector rotation has durable legs.
